clue.text: Welsh are agreed about English film

indicators.note: 'about' here means turned around and moved about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the bulk of the letters to shuffle
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Some Welsh people reach agreement over an English film.
explanation.walkthrough: The E for English joins the fodder too. WHERE EAGLES DARE is a 1968 war film with Richard Burton, himself Welsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Where Eagles Dare is a classic Second World War adventure movie, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Lynx perhaps excited about ocelot's tail

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the cat's name is kept

blocks.note: wild means frenzied or excited
CA is short for circa, about
the last letter of ocelot

explanation.surface: A lynx gets worked up about an ocelot's tail, as one wild cat to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives CA (circa) rather than signalling a shuffle or a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A lynx is one species of wildcat, so 'perhaps' flags it as an example of the class.

clue.text: Cheer meal, regularly consumed

indicators.note: 'regularly' means at even intervals, so every second letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of meal
consumed food means ate

explanation.surface: A meal eaten at regular times lifts the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate someone is to cheer them up, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Short Harper Lee novel entertains Mike in passing

indicators.note: something cut short loses its final letter
'novel' in the sense of new means the letters take a fresh arrangement
to entertain is to hold or host, so one thing goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then shortened by its last letter
taken as written
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Harper Lee's brief novel features a character called Mike, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harper Lee novel' suggests To Kill a Mockingbird, but 'novel' is the shuffle signal; HARPE and LEE are mixed and M sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing is transient or short-lived, which is what ephemeral means.

clue.text: Appearance by Sting that makes things feel cooler?

blocks.note: an air is a manner or appearance
a sting is a swindle, a con

explanation.surface: A performance by the singer Sting is so good it gives people the chills.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting looks like the musician; he is just a swindle here. The definition describes the machine by what it does.
explanation.definitionFit: Air conditioning is the equipment that chills a room, so it is what makes things cooler.

clue.text: Liberal taking home instruction

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
earning is taking home pay

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician brings work home with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking home' reads like taking work home but means earning, as in take-home pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is education or teaching received, a synonym of instruction.

clue.text: Mum with ring returned to display

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these letters are read from the end

blocks.note: mum means silent, and SH is the call for silence
W is short for with
a ring is shaped like O

explanation.surface: A mother's ring is sent back to be put on display.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum looks like a mother but means quiet, hence SH; only W and O are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to show it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Cut top from wooden beam and pack in part of ship

indicators.note: cutting the top off a word in a down clue removes its first letter

blocks.note: a rafter is a wooden roof beam, here losing its first letter
a pack of cards is a deck

explanation.surface: Instructions to trim a timber beam and stow it aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The afterdeck is the deck at the stern of a vessel, so it is one part of a ship.

clue.text: Copper's one suspicion

blocks.note: first meaning: copper is a chemical ...
second meaning: a trace or hint

explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer with a hunch; it is the metal Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a chemical element, and an element can also mean a slight trace or suggestion of something.

clue.text: Hide article penned by king

indicators.note: something penned by another is shut inside it, like an animal in a pen

blocks.note: King Lear of Shakespeare
the definite article

explanation.surface: Instruction to conceal a piece of writing that a monarch composed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal skin, and a hide is such a skin.

clue.text: Champion beer gathers support

indicators.note: to gather is to collect around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
a post is a supporting upright

explanation.surface: A prize-winning beer is attracting backers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' looks like an adjective praising the beer; it is the noun meaning advocate.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a leading advocate of a cause, a champion of it.

clue.text: Cake best with bit of butter?

blocks.note: the cream is the best of something
a butter is something that butts, like a goat, and its horn is the part it butts with

explanation.surface: The finest cake is made with a little butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of butter' reads as a knob of the dairy spread; the question mark flags a butter as a creature that butts. A cream horn is a cone of puff pastry filled with cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream horn is a pastry, a kind of small cake sold in British bakeries.

clue.text: Encourage Rush to cut intro

indicators.note: the intro is the opening, so cutting it removes the first letter

blocks.note: a surge is a sudden rush

explanation.surface: Someone asks the band Rush to shorten a song's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to push or encourage them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Tense and irritable when getting cropped top

indicators.note: cropped means trimmed short, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
shirty is British slang for bad-tempered, here losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone gets nervy and cross when made to wear a crop top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cropped top' looks like one garment; the clue splits it. Shirty is informal British for annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shirt is a garment for the upper body, which is what a top is.

clue.text: England defenders once wary of Germans crossing on the wing?

definitions.text: England defenders once wary of Germans crossing on the wing?

blocks.clueFragment: England defenders once wary of Germans crossing on the wing?
blocks.note: surface reading: former England football defenders nervous of German wingers putting in crosses

blocks.clueFragment: England defenders once wary of Germans crossing on the wing?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the wartime volunteer force watching for German aircraft or paratroopers flying over

explanation.walkthrough: Football words (defenders, crossing, wing) disguise the Second World War: the Home Guard was Britain's volunteer home-defence force, alert to German invasion from the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Guard defended Britain in the Second World War against a German invasion, including by air.

clue.text: Spotless pub, once derelict, beginning to trend

indicators.note: derelict means fallen into ruin, so the letters are left in disorder
the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
taken as written, then rearranged
first letter of trend

explanation.surface: A formerly run-down pub, now spotless, is starting to become fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless figuratively means blameless or free of guilt, as innocent does.

clue.text: Spoiled, one raged about a fizzy drink

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined and messed up, so the letters are jumbled
'about' means around, so the jumbled letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: these words rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spoilt child flies into a temper over a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a carbonated orange-flavoured soft drink, so it is a fizzy drink.

clue.text: Register is wrong, with too much written up

indicators.note: in a down entry, writing upwards means the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: false means wrong
OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: An official record is inaccurate and overwritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Register' looks like a list of names; it is a vocal range.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a vocal register above the singer's normal voice.

clue.text: Heading west, part of trail I'm after is close

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them
in an across entry west is leftwards, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: a run of letters found inside these words

explanation.surface: A walker heading west follows part of a trail they are close to finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Close as in intimate: a familiar friend is a close one.

clue.text: Female left after United crumbled in first half turning point?

indicators.note: 'after' places the first letter behind the next, so they are joined in that order
keeping only the first half means the back half of the word is dropped

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written, then cut to its first four letters

explanation.surface: A woman leaves after Manchester United fall apart in the first half, the turning point of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal sense: a lever turns on a fulcrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A fulcrum is the pivot on which a lever turns, so it is literally a turning point.

clue.text: In the auditorium, convention is crammed

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a pact is an agreement or convention

explanation.surface: A conference audience fills the hall to bursting.
explanation.definitionFit: Packed and crammed both mean filled tightly to capacity.

clue.text: Untouched grey not good, dyed in new style

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to leave out the abbreviation for good
a new style is a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then losing G
G is the abbreviation for good, removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hair left grey looks bad, so it is coloured in a new style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untouched' suggests hair not dyed; it means emotionally unmoved.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dry-eyed is not crying, emotionally unmoved by a sad event.

clue.text: Sleeve with hole where deodorant's applied

blocks.note: the arm of a garment is its sleeve
a pit is a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: A shirt sleeve with a hole in the very spot where deodorant goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Deodorant is sprayed or rolled under the arm, and that hollow is the armpit.

clue.text: Pins on badges at last

indicators.note: 'at last' points to the final letter only

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
last letter of badges

explanation.surface: Pins are attached to badges as the final step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pins' suggests badge fastenings; it is slang for legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pins is informal British slang for legs.

clue.text: Playful girl with shy pet sadly lacking energy

indicators.note: 'lacking' means missing something, so a letter is left out
'sadly' suggests things going badly, so the letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, then losing E
E is the physics symbol for energy, removed

explanation.surface: A lively girl whose timid pet is sadly listless.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and full of spirit, close to playful.

clue.text: Bat upside down over ball? Not acceptable

indicators.note: in a down entry upside down means the letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over
a ball is round, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A cricket bat held upside down for a delivery would be against the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is something forbidden by custom, so a taboo subject is socially unacceptable.

clue.text: Cry my red Lilo needs scrubbing occasionally

indicators.note: scrubbing out letters now and then removes every other one, leaving the rest

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A grubby red inflatable mattress needs washing now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lilo is a British brand of inflatable airbed for the beach or pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A yell is a loud shout, a cry.

clue.text: Chemical compound maybe concerning American chap

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
A is the abbreviation for American
a gent is a gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: A chemical compound perhaps of interest to an American man.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance used to produce a reaction, often a chemical compound, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Rogue duck in quiet parking place

indicators.note: 'in' places the first item inside the place that follows

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a lay-by is a roadside pull-in for parking
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A wayward duck sits in a quiet car park.
explanation.walkthrough: A lay-by is a British roadside stopping area.
explanation.definitionFit: A playboy is a pleasure-seeking man, a charming rogue.

clue.text: Where reflective studs are in a way colourless

definitions.text: Where reflective studs are in a way

blocks.clueFragment: Where reflective studs are in a way
blocks.note: first meaning: cat's eyes are set along the centre line of a road
second meaning: bland, moderate, unexciting

explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' looks like 'somewhat' but means on a road. Cat's eyes are the reflective studs set in British roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflective studs sit along the centre line of a road, and middle-of-the-road also describes anything moderate and bland.
